examples.en: My friends sat in a circle around the table.
I went all the way around the park and broke a sweat.
The kids gathered in a ring around the teacher.

examples.ko: 집 주변에 나무를 삥 둘러 심었어요.
examples.en: We planted trees in a ring around the house.

examples.ko: 갑자기 어지러워서 방이 삥 도는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: I suddenly felt dizzy, as if the room were spinning.

examples.ko: 길을 몰라서 같은 동네를 삥 돌아서 왔어요.
examples.en: I didn't know the way, so I came around the same neighborhood in a loop.

explain: 둥글게 한 바퀴 도는 모양이나 빙 둘러서 있는 모양에 써요. '빙'보다 조금 센 느낌이 있어요. 어지러울 때는 '핑 돌다'를 더 흔히 써요.

phrases.en: The children stood in a circle around the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 한 곳을 둥글게 둘러싸고 서 있는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes many people standing in a ring around one spot.

phrases.en: I went around the playground and then went home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 바퀴 크게 도는 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes going around once in a big loop.

phrases.en: People surrounded the singer in a ring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 사람이나 물건을 빙 둘러서 에워쌀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people or things form a ring around someone or something.

explain_en: It describes going once around in a circle or standing in a ring. It feels slightly stronger than '빙'. For dizziness, '핑 돌다' is more common.

t90.ax: My friends sat in a circle around the table.

en: to be strange; to be odd; to be quirky

examples.en: This food smells a bit odd.
I heard a strange sound and looked behind me.
Since yesterday the machine has been acting weird.
That person's outfit looked strange.
I thought it looked odd, but it tasted good when I tried it.

examples.ko: 꿈이 너무 요상해서 친구한테 얘기해 줬어요.
examples.en: My dream was so weird that I told my friend about it.

explain: '이상하다'보다 입말 느낌이 강하고, 조금 장난스럽거나 못마땅한 느낌이 들어요. 글이나 발표보다 편한 대화에서 어울려요. '요상한 + 명사', '요상하게 + 동사'로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: There is a strange smell from the kitchen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 가장 기본적인 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic form for describing a noun.

phrases.en: That fruit has a strange shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'로 바꿔서 뒤의 동사를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Changes to '-게' to describe the verb that follows.

phrases.en: The taste isn't as strange as I thought.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 '이상하지 않다'는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means 'not strange'.

explain_en: It feels more colloquial than '이상하다' and can sound a bit playful or disapproving. It fits casual conversation better than writing or presentations. It is often used as '요상한 + noun' or '요상하게 + verb'.

t90.ax: This food smells a bit odd.

examples.ko: 방바닥이 절절 끓어서 앉아 있기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The floor is boiling hot, so it's hard to sit.
In winter, an ondol room is best when the floor is piping hot.
I lay down on the scorching floor at the sauna.

examples.ko: 아랫목이 절절 끓어서 이불 속이 따뜻해요.
examples.en: The warmest spot of the room is so hot that it's cozy under the blanket.

examples.ko: 보일러를 세게 틀었더니 바닥이 절절 끓어요.
examples.en: I turned the boiler up high, and now the floor is blazing hot.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 아랫목은 늘 절절 끓었어요.
examples.en: The warmest spot in Grandma's house was always scorching hot.

explain: 주로 '절절 끓다'로 방바닥이 아주 뜨거울 때 써요. '절절하다'와 소리는 비슷하지만 감정을 말하는 게 아니라 뜨거운 느낌을 말해요.

phrases.en: In winter the warmest spot on the floor is boiling hot and cozy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 온돌방에서 가장 따뜻한 자리가 아주 뜨거울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the warmest spot of a heated floor is very hot.

phrases.en: I rested well in the piping hot room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '절절 끓다'를 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.en: The floor is nice and hot, so I feel good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '절절'보다 덜 강하고 기분 좋게 따뜻한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gentler than '절절' and suggests a pleasant warmth.

explain_en: It is mainly used as '절절 끓다' when a floor is extremely hot. It sounds similar to '절절하다', but it describes heat, not emotion.

examples.en: Please don't tease me for acting silly at my age.
Dad embarrassed me again by acting out of line.
Crying all of a sudden, I am being silly.

examples.ko: 할머니는 주책없이 큰 소리로 노래를 부르셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother sang loudly without any sense of occasion.

examples.ko: 회식에서 주책 부리는 상사 때문에 민망했어요.
examples.en: I felt awkward because my boss was acting inappropriately at the company dinner.
Everyone laughed because of the silly behavior.

explain: 상황이나 나이에 맞지 않게 말하고 행동하는 모습을 가볍게 놀리거나 흉볼 때 써요. '주책이다', '주책을 떨다', '주책 부리다'처럼 쓰고, '주책없다'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I'm being tactless again, I'm sorry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 행동을 부끄러워하며 말할 때 써요. 남에게 쓰면 흉보는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when feeling embarrassed about your own behavior. About others, it sounds like teasing.

phrases.en: Tears are coming out at the wrong time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주책'과 거의 같은 뜻이에요. '주책없이'로 행동 앞에 자주 붙어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 주책. Often appears as 주책없이 before an action.

phrases.en: Please don't act out of place at the company dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황에 맞지 않게 행동한다는 뜻이에요. '주책을 떨다'와 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means acting in a way that doesn't fit the situation. Similar to 주책을 떨다.

explain_en: It is used to lightly tease or criticize someone who talks or acts in a way that does not fit the situation or their age. It appears as '주책이다', '주책을 떨다', and '주책 부리다', and '주책없다' is very often used with almost the same meaning.

en: to treat; to buy a meal

examples.en: I got paid, so I'll treat you today.
I treated my team members to celebrate my promotion.
If you passed, you have to treat us!
My friend got a job and decided to treat us.
The person who treats is the one who pays.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 제가 점심 한턱낼 테니 오세요.
examples.en: I'll treat you to lunch this weekend, so come over.

explain: 좋은 일이 있을 때 다른 사람들에게 음식이나 술자리 등을 대접하는 말이에요. 말할 때는 '한턱 쏘다'라고도 해요. 그냥 밥값을 나눠 내는 것과 달리 한 사람이 기쁨을 나누며 사는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Today I'll treat everyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 표현이라 친구나 동료에게 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual spoken expression that suits friends and coworkers.

phrases.en: If I pass the test, I'll treat you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 대접하겠다고 약속할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to promise that you will treat someone.

phrases.en: You got a job, so you should treat us!
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 일이 생긴 사람에게 대접해 달라고 장난스럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Playfully asking someone with good news to treat everyone.

explain_en: Treat friends to food or drinks to celebrate; casual. It means to treat others to a meal or outing when something good happens. In speech people also say '한턱 쏘다'. Unlike splitting the bill, it feels like one person paying to share their happiness.

t90.ax: I got paid, so I'll treat you today.

en: to get a windfall; to strike it rich

examples.en: I found ten thousand won on the street, what a windfall.
Winning the lottery, you really struck it rich.

examples.ko: 중고 가게에서 새 책을 싸게 사서 횡재한 기분이에요.
examples.en: I bought a new book cheaply at a used shop and feel like I got a bargain.

examples.ko: 오늘 횡재할 것 같은 느낌이 들어요.
examples.en: I have a feeling I'll get lucky today.
I got a movie ticket for free, so I think I hit the jackpot.

examples.ko: 횡재하고 싶다고 복권만 사면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't only buy lottery tickets just because you want a windfall.

explain: 애쓰지 않았는데 뜻밖에 돈이나 물건 같은 이득을 얻었을 때 써요. 그냥 '운이 좋다'보다 얻은 것이 눈에 보일 때 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '횡재했다!'처럼 기쁜 마음을 바로 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: You got it at half price? What a windfall!
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람의 뜻밖의 행운을 보고 놀라거나 축하할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to react with surprise or congratulations to someone else's unexpected luck.

phrases.example: 오랜만에 친구가 밥을 사 줘서 횡재한 기분이에요.
phrases.en: I feel like I hit the jackpot because my friend treated me to a meal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 이득은 아니어도 뜻밖의 행운을 느낄 때 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works even for a small, unexpected piece of luck.
phrases.en_equiv: feeling like I struck it lucky

phrases.example: 이 가격에 이 가방이라니, 완전 횡재예요!
phrases.en: This bag at this price is a total steal!
phrases.nuance_ko: '횡재'를 명사로 쓴 말이에요. '완전'을 붙이면 대화체로 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 횡재 as a noun. Adding 완전 makes it sound conversational.

explain_en: Use it when you unexpectedly gain something like money or an item without trying hard. It fits better than just '운이 좋다' when there is a visible gain. In speech, people often exclaim it right away, like '횡재했다!'.

en: to keep tilting (one's head) from side to side

examples.en: He tilted his head back and forth and thought for a long time.

examples.ko: 아이가 이해가 안 되는지 머리를 갸우뚱거려요.
examples.en: The child keeps tilting her head as if she doesn't understand.

examples.ko: 왜 그런지 몰라서 계속 고개를 갸우뚱거렸어요.
examples.en: I didn't know why, so I kept tilting my head.
The students started tilting their heads at the problem.
Don't just tilt your head; if you don't know, ask right away.

examples.ko: 강아지가 소리를 듣고 갸우뚱거리는 모습이 귀여워요.
examples.en: The puppy tilting its head at the sound is cute.

explain: '고개를 갸우뚱거리다'처럼 주로 고개와 같이 쓰고, 모르겠거나 이상할 때 보이는 반응이에요. '갸웃거리다'와 거의 같은 상황에서 써요. 한 번만 기울일 때는 '갸우뚱하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling looked at me, tilting their head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 거의 같은 뜻이라 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as the headword and interchangeable with it.

phrases.en: He tilted his head and thought for a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 달리 고개를 한 번만 기울일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike the headword, it describes tilting the head just once.

phrases.en: The way they tilt their head is cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어를 '-는' 형태로 바꿔 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The headword in its modifier form, attached to a noun that follows.

explain_en: It is mostly used with '고개' as in '고개를 갸우뚱거리다', a reaction when someone doesn't get it or finds something odd. It is used in nearly the same situations as '갸웃거리다'. For tilting just once, '갸우뚱하다' is used.

t90.ax: I didn't know why, so I kept tilting my head.

en: to come rolling in; to fall into one's lap

examples.en: A ball suddenly rolled into the yard.

examples.ko: 하늘에서 복이 굴러들어 온 것 같아요.
examples.en: It feels like good luck has dropped right into my lap.

examples.ko: 신발 속에 작은 돌이 굴러들어 가서 아파요.
examples.en: A small stone rolled into my shoe, so it hurts.

examples.ko: 뜻밖의 큰돈이 굴러들어 와서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A large sum of money came to me unexpectedly, and I was shocked.

examples.ko: 이런 좋은 기회가 저절로 굴러들지는 않아요.
examples.en: A good opportunity like this doesn't just fall into your lap.

examples.ko: 얼마 전에 굴러든 신입이 일을 제일 잘해요.
examples.en: The newcomer who recently turned up out of nowhere works the best.

explain: 공이나 돌처럼 실제로 굴러서 들어올 때도 쓰지만, 복이나 돈, 기회가 뜻밖에 생길 때 '굴러들어 오다'라고 많이 말해요. 비슷한 속담 '굴러온 돌이 박힌 돌 빼낸다'에는 '굴러오다'가 쓰여요.

phrases.en: This chance is a piece of luck that fell into my lap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 애쓰지 않았는데 생긴 좋은 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for good luck that came without effort.

phrases.en: The ball rolled into the hole.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오다' 대신 '가다'를 쓰면 안쪽으로 굴러 들어가는 방향을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 가다 instead of 오다, it shows rolling inward away from the speaker.

phrases.en: It was unexpected money that came my way, so I was happy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획 없이 생긴 돈을 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to describe money that arrived unexpectedly.
phrases.en_equiv: money that came out of nowhere

explain_en: It is used when something really rolls in, like a ball or stone, but people often say '굴러들어 오다' when luck, money or an opportunity comes unexpectedly. The related proverb '굴러온 돌이 박힌 돌 빼낸다' uses '굴러오다' instead.

examples.en: Grandmother is drawing water from the well.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 샘에서 물을 긷는 일로 하루를 시작했어요.
examples.en: The villagers began the day by drawing water from the spring.

examples.ko: 물을 긷지 않아도 집에서 수도를 틀면 돼요.
examples.en: You don't have to draw water; just turn on the tap at home.
The well is deep, so it's hard to draw water.

examples.ko: 양동이로 물을 긷고 나서 밥을 지었어요.
examples.en: After drawing water with a bucket, I cooked rice.

examples.ko: 아버지가 물을 긷던 우물이 아직 마을에 있어요.
examples.en: The well where my father used to draw water is still in the village.

explain: 우물이나 샘에서 물을 퍼 올릴 때 쓰는 말이라 요즘은 옛날이야기나 시골 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요. ㄷ 불규칙이라 '길어요, 길은, 길으면'으로 바뀌고 '긷고, 긷지, 긷는'은 그대로예요. 형용사 '길다'의 '길어요'와 모양이 같아서 문장 속 뜻으로 구별해요.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 매일 아침 우물물을 길었어요.
phrases.en: When I was young, I drew well water every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '긷다'의 가장 기본 짝말이고, 과거형은 '길었어요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing; note the past form changes to 길었어요.

phrases.en: Every morning I fetch water from the spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어' 앞에서는 '길어'로 바뀌어요. 물을 떠서 가져온다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before -아/어 it becomes 길어. It means drawing water and bringing it back.

phrases.example: 요즘은 수도가 있어서 물을 긷지 않아요.
phrases.en: These days we have taps, so nobody draws water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자음 앞에서는 '긷-'이 그대로여서 '긷지'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a consonant the stem stays 긷-, so it is 긷지.

explain_en: Scoop water from a well (우물에서 물을 긷다) It is used for drawing water from a well or spring, so today it appears more in old tales and stories of the countryside. It is a ㄷ-irregular verb: it changes to 길어요, 길은, 길으면, while 긷고, 긷지, 긷는 stay the same. '길어요' looks identical to that of the adjective '길다' (long), so tell them apart by context.

t90.ax: Grandmother is drawing water from the well.

en: to jump; to hop; to skip

examples.en: The rabbit hops around in the meadow.
The child ran over hopping with excitement.
The puppy started bouncing when it saw its owner.
The frog hopped around and then plopped into the pond.
My younger sibling bounced up and down after getting a present.

examples.ko: 깡충거리는 아이들을 보니 저도 기분이 좋아져요.
examples.en: Watching the kids hop about makes me feel good too.

explain: 토끼나 작은 동물, 아이처럼 작고 가볍게 짧게 뛰는 모습에 써요. 크고 시원하게 뛰는 모양은 '껑충껑충'으로 말해요. '깡충깡충 뛰다'처럼 쓰는 경우도 많아요.

phrases.en: The kids are so excited they hop around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 몸으로 가볍게 반복해서 뛰는 모습이에요. '깡충거리다'와 같은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Small, light, repeated hops, with the same feel as '깡충거리다'.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is in a good mood and skips along.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 다른 동작과 함께 이어서 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-며' you can join it with another action.

phrases.en: The rabbit hops when it sees a carrot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깡충거리다'와 같은 뜻이에요. 말에서는 '-거리다'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '깡충거리다'. '-거리다' is more common in speech.

explain_en: Small light hops, like a rabbit or a small child. It describes small, light, short hops by rabbits, small animals or children. A bigger, longer leap is described with '껑충껑충'. People also often say '깡충깡충 뛰다'.

t90.ax: The rabbit hops around in the meadow.

examples.en: The child was startled and let out a shriek.
The duck quacked loudly and ran away.

examples.ko: 갑자기 뒤에서 꽥 소리를 질러서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Someone suddenly yelled behind me and I was startled.

examples.ko: 동생이 화가 나서 나한테 꽥 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling got angry and yelled at me.

examples.ko: 거위가 낯선 사람을 보고 꽥 울었어요.
examples.en: The goose honked sharply when it saw a stranger.

examples.ko: 아버지가 갑자기 꽥 하고 화를 내셔서 모두 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: Dad suddenly snapped angrily, and everyone went quiet.

explain: 갑자기 크고 날카롭게 나는 소리를 나타내요. '꽥 소리를 지르다', '꽥 하고 화를 내다'처럼 쓰고, 오리나 거위 소리에도 써요. 소리가 이어지면 '꽥꽥'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 오리들이 꽥꽥 울면서 물 위를 헤엄쳐요.
phrases.en: The ducks swim on the water, quacking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽥'이 한 번이라면 '꽥꽥'은 소리가 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 꽥 is a single sound; 꽥꽥 is for a continued sound.

phrases.en: I screamed when I saw a cockroach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 크고 날카롭게 소리칠 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for a sudden loud, sharp scream.

phrases.example: 동생이 꽥 하고 화를 내서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling suddenly snapped angrily and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 크게 소리 내며 화를 내는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes suddenly snapping at someone with a loud voice.

explain_en: It describes a sudden, loud, sharp sound. You say '꽥 소리를 지르다' or '꽥 하고 화를 내다', and it also fits ducks and geese. For a repeated sound, use '꽥꽥'.

t90.ax: The duck quacked loudly and ran away.

examples.ko: 바쁜데도 그를 만나려고 부러 시간을 낸 거예요.
examples.en: Even though I was busy, I made time on purpose to meet him.
He passed by pretending not to know on purpose.

examples.ko: 친구가 부러 큰 소리로 웃어 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend laughed loudly on purpose to cheer me up.

examples.ko: 저는 부러 먼 길로 돌아서 갔어요.
examples.en: I deliberately took the long way around.
I didn't say it that way on purpose.

examples.ko: 그녀는 부러 늦게 도착한 것처럼 보였어요.
examples.en: She seemed to have arrived late on purpose.

explain: '일부러'와 뜻이 같은 부사예요. 입말에서는 '일부러'가 자연스럽고, '부러'는 글이나 오래된 말투에서 가끔 보여요. 학습자는 '일부러'를 쓰면 돼요.

phrases.en: I spoke loudly on purpose.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부러'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 '일부러'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 부러; use 일부러 when speaking.

phrases.en: I made a special trip to see my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 시간을 내서 누구를 만나러 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you take the trouble to go and see someone.
phrases.en_equiv: to go out of one's way to visit

phrases.en: I didn't do it on purpose, I'm sorry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실수했을 때 사과하면서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when apologizing for a mistake.
phrases.en_equiv: I didn't do it on purpose

explain_en: An adverb with the same meaning as '일부러'. In speech '일부러' sounds natural; '부러' appears occasionally in writing or old-fashioned speech. As a learner, just use '일부러'.

en: to decay; to wear thin; to molder

examples.en: The old clothesline wore out from the rain.
Salted seafood has to ferment well to get a deep flavor.

examples.ko: 화가 났지만 시간이 지나니까 마음이 삭았어요.
examples.en: I was angry, but as time passed my anger subsided.

examples.ko: 창고에 둔 가죽 끈이 삭아서 끊어졌어요.
examples.en: The leather strap I kept in the storage room rotted and snapped.

examples.ko: 땅속에 묻은 낙엽이 천천히 삭고 있어요.
examples.en: The fallen leaves buried in the ground are slowly decomposing.

examples.ko: 속이 아직 안 삭았는지 배가 불러요.
examples.en: My stomach still feels full, as if the food hasn't digested yet.

explain: '화가 삭다'처럼 마음이 가라앉는 뜻과 '젓갈이 삭다', '옷감이 삭다'처럼 서서히 변하는 뜻이 있어요. '썩다'는 아주 상해 버린 느낌이고, '삭다'는 시간이 지나 천천히 변하는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: As time passed, my anger died down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음속 화나 분노가 천천히 가라앉는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means anger slowly calms down.

phrases.en: The old fabric had worn thin and tore easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래되어 천이 약해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cloth becomes weak with age.

phrases.en: The worn-out rope suddenly snapped.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삭은'은 오래돼서 약해진 물건 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 삭은 goes before something that has become weak with age.

explain_en: It covers both feelings that settle down (화가 삭다) and things that slowly break down, like fermenting seafood or worn fabric. 썩다 sounds fully spoiled, while 삭다 describes a gradual change over time.

examples.en: My friends are whispering at the back of the classroom.
The kids are whispering behind the teacher's back.
What are you two whispering about?
The sound of whispering in the theater bothered me a little.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 구석에서 속닥거리다가 웃음을 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: The two were whispering in the corner and then burst out laughing.

examples.ko: 동생들이 밤새 속닥거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My younger siblings whispered all night, so I couldn't sleep.

explain: 작은 목소리로 은밀하게 계속 이야기하는 모습에 써요. 비슷한 말로 '소곤거리다'가 있고, 활용은 '속닥거려요', '속닥거리는'이에요.

phrases.en: Students whisper in the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: '속닥거리다'와 비슷하지만 비밀스러운 느낌이 조금 덜해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'soktakgeorida' but with a bit less sense of secrecy.

phrases.en: I woke up to the sound of whispering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 올 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form used before a noun.

phrases.en: Please don't whisper during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용히 하라고 부탁할 때 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite negative request used to ask someone to stop whispering.

explain_en: Near-synonym of 소곤거리다; whispering in a hushed, secretive way, often by a few people. It describes talking on and on in a small, secretive voice. '소곤거리다' is a similar word, and it conjugates as '속닥거려요' and '속닥거리는'.

t90.ax: What are you two whispering about?
